clues.rationale: Quoted inside the same header snippet the trials used to reach the PostgreSQL port, and it scopes the alert to internally hosted database or web hosts. Deployment context only, and untargetable because no accepted generic operator rewrites rule-header addresses. Suite negative N-wrong-destination-address.

clues.description: Content "|40|RSYNCD|3a|", the @RSYNCD: daemon protocol greeting.
clues.provenance: dataset-clue-baseline-v2 review packet candidate et-2067354-baseline (packet sha256 7a9c9e97...); trials 0-2 rule_evidence content:"|40|RSYNCD|3a|"; suite negative N-banner-changed; manual review calibration review notes
clues.rationale: Identifies the rsync daemon protocol outright, which is the product half of the vulnerability and the reason all three v2 trials opened with it and all three predicted the target exactly. It is also the clue the rest of the rule is relative to, since the byte tests are positioned from the negotiation that follows it. Suite negative N-banner-changed removes the greeting.

clues.description: byte_test:4,>,16,9,relative,little with byte_test:4,<,65,9,relative,little, a little-endian four-byte field at offset 9 constrained to the range 17 through 64.
clues.provenance: dataset-clue-baseline-v2 review packet candidate et-2067354-baseline (packet sha256 7a9c9e97...); trials 0-2 quoted byte_test:4,>,16,9,relative,little; and byte_test:4,<,65,9,relative,little; in one clue; suite negatives N-seed-length-at-lower-bound and N-seed-length-at-upper-bound
clues.rationale: The exploit condition: the overflow is reached when the attacker-controlled checksum length exceeds the fixed sixteen-byte digest buffer. All three v2 trials called this bounded window the decisive condition or the key exploit indicator and reasoned from it to the CVE. The two tests are a single range check expressed as two options and every trial quoted them together, so they are one inference unit. Suite negatives N-seed-length-at-lower-bound and N-seed-length-at-upper-bound pin both edges.

clues.description: Contents "--server" and "--sender".
clues.provenance: dataset-clue-baseline-v2 review packet candidate et-2067354-baseline (packet sha256 7a9c9e97...); trials 0-2 reported content:"--server"; and content:"--sender"; in one clue; suite negatives N-server-argument-changed and N-sender-argument-changed
clues.rationale: Places the daemon in the server-sender role in which it parses the client-supplied checksum metadata, which is the reachability condition for the overflow. All three v2 trials reported the two arguments as a single clue about operating mode, so they are one inference unit. Ranked third because mode selection is ordinary rsync traffic until the length window at rank 2 is also present. Suite negatives N-server-argument-changed and N-sender-argument-changed.

clues.description: Rule header destination port 873.
clues.provenance: dataset-clue-baseline-v2 review packet candidate et-2067354-baseline (packet sha256 7a9c9e97...); trials 0-2 rule_evidence alert tcp any any -> $HOME_NET 873; suite negative N-wrong-port
clues.rationale: The registered rsync daemon port; every v2 trial quoted the header line together with the banner when establishing that this is rsync traffic. It corroborates a service the banner already names, so it stays secondary despite being one of the few directly targetable header facets in the corpus. Suite negative N-wrong-port moves the traffic to an adjacent port.

clues.description: Contents "|00 00 07|" and "|0e|", the message framing marker and the checksum negotiation tag byte.
clues.provenance: dataset-clue-baseline-v2 review packet candidate et-2067354-baseline (packet sha256 7a9c9e97...); trials 0-2 quoted content:"|00 00 07|"; and content:"|0e|"; together; suite negatives N-framing-marker-changed and N-negotiation-tag-changed
clues.rationale: Locates the negotiation message that the byte tests read their offsets from. All three v2 trials quoted the two bytes together while describing a crafted protocol structure rather than a banner match. The tag byte is structurally untargetable because its distance:0 successor depends on it, while the framing marker is targetable. Suite negatives N-framing-marker-changed and N-negotiation-tag-changed.

clues.description: distance:0 requiring the negotiation tag to follow the framing marker immediately.
clues.provenance: dataset-clue-baseline-v2 review packet candidate et-2067354-baseline (packet sha256 7a9c9e97...); trials 1 and 2 quoted content:"|0e|"; distance:0;; suite negative N-tag-before-framing-marker
clues.rationale: Ordering constraint that binds the framing pair into a single protocol message. v2 trials 1 and 2 quoted it inline with the tag byte. It is layout mechanics rather than an independent inference, so it is secondary. Suite negative N-tag-before-framing-marker.

clues.description: byte_test:1,&,0x80,0,relative requiring the high bit of the byte after the tag to be set.
clues.provenance: dataset-clue-baseline-v2 review packet candidate et-2067354-baseline (packet sha256 7a9c9e97...); trials 1 and 2 quoted byte_test:1,&,0x80,0,relative; with the length window; suite negative N-flag-high-bit-clear
clues.rationale: A protocol flag check that v2 trials 1 and 2 grouped with the length window when describing the exploit condition. It is a single-bit flag rather than the overflow condition itself, so it is recorded as supporting structure. Suite negative N-flag-high-bit-clear.

clues.description: flow:established,to_server restricting the match to a client request into the daemon.
clues.provenance: dataset-clue-baseline-v2 review packet candidate et-2067354-baseline (packet sha256 7a9c9e97...); trial 2 rule_evidence flow:established,to_server; as a standalone clue; suite negatives N-flow-not-established and N-wrong-direction
clues.rationale: v2 trial 2 gave the flow its own clue, reading it as an established client-to-server request into the protected rsync daemon. Transport context that carries no product content beyond what the port and banner already give. Suite negatives N-flow-not-established and N-wrong-direction.
